en.name: Water spinach
en.summary: Water spinach is the hollow-stemmed green sold in big loose bunches and cooked hard and fast with garlic. In a home fridge expect about 3–5 days. Its published optimum is a cool room rather than a cold one, and it takes chilling injury at refrigerator temperatures, which is why the home figure is deliberately short.
en.pantry: There is no room-temperature timeline for water spinach. Left out it wilts within hours, and the leaves go limp long before the stems do. Postharvest guidance puts its ideal holding temperature at 12–14 °C (54–57 °F) with high humidity — cooler than a Taiwanese kitchen and warmer than a fridge — which is a condition most homes simply do not have.
en.fridge: Bag the bunch to stop water loss and keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where about 3–5 days is realistic. The published optimum needs a 12–14 °C (54–57 °F) cold room, and the same guidance warns that ung choi is injured below roughly 10–14 °C (50–57 °F), with leaves and stems darkening near freezing — so a home fridge shortens its life rather than extending it. Do not pack it on ice, do not wash it before storing, and put it in the warmest part of the fridge you have.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published for water spinach, and freezing raw bunches is not worth doing — the hollow stems collapse and the leaves thaw to a dark slime. If you are left with too much, cook it first and eat the dish within a few days rather than trying to store the raw vegetable. This is a green to buy in the quantity you will cook this week.
spoilage: Leaves darkening to grey-green or black, which on this vegetable is often cold damage rather than age
Slimy patches at the cut ends or where the bunch was tied
Hollow stems gone soft, flattened or watery
A sour, swampy smell instead of a clean green one
tips: Buy it the day or two before you plan to cook it; it does not reward stockpiling.
Keep it bagged — most of the loss here is water, not spoilage.
Use the warmest shelf or drawer in the fridge, not the coldest.
Separate leaves from stems when cooking; the stems need a head start.

faq.q: How long does water spinach last in the fridge?
faq.a: About 3–5 days bagged at 4 °C or below. It is chilling-sensitive, so a cold fridge does not give it the life a cool room would.

faq.q: Why does water spinach go black in the fridge?
faq.a: It takes chilling injury below roughly 10–14 °C, which darkens the leaves and stems. That is cold damage, not ordinary spoilage.
There is no published timeline and raw freezing gives poor results. Cook it and eat the dish instead.

faq.q: Should you wash water spinach before storing it?
faq.a: No. Wash it just before cooking; surface water accelerates slime at the cut ends.

zh.name: 空心菜
zh.summary: 空心菜就是那種一大把賣、莖中空、要用大火快炒配蒜頭的青菜。家用冰箱大約可放 3～5 天。它的最佳保存溫度其實是「涼」而不是「冷」，而且在冷藏溫度下會出現低溫傷害，所以家用的天數刻意抓得比較短。
zh.pantry: 空心菜沒有常溫保存的天數。放在外面幾小時就軟掉，葉子又比莖更早陣亡。採後處理的建議是把它放在 12～14 °C、高濕度的環境——比台灣的廚房涼，又比冰箱溫暖——而這是大多數家庭根本沒有的條件。
zh.fridge: 整把裝袋防止失水，放在 4 °C 以下，實際上大約 3～5 天。已發表的最佳條件需要 12～14 °C 的冷藏庫房，同一份資料也警告空心菜在大約 10～14 °C 以下就會受到低溫傷害，接近冰點時葉與莖都會變黑——所以家用冰箱是在縮短它的壽命，而不是延長。不要鋪冰，不要洗過再放，並且放在冰箱裡溫度最高的位置。
zh.freezer: 空心菜沒有已發表的冷凍期限，生凍也不值得——中空的莖會塌掉，葉子解凍後只剩一團暗色黏糊。買太多的話，不如先炒好，並在幾天內把菜吃完，而不是想辦法保存生的。這是一種「這週吃多少就買多少」的青菜。
spoilage: 葉子轉成灰綠或發黑，在這種菜上多半是低溫傷害而不是老化
切口處或綁束處出現黏滑
中空的莖變軟、壓扁或出水
聞起來發酸、有水塘味，而不是清爽的青草味
tips: 要炒的前一兩天再買，它不適合囤貨。
務必裝袋——它主要的損耗是失水，不是腐敗。
放冰箱裡最不冷的那一層或那一格，不要放最冷處。
下鍋時葉與梗分開，梗要先下。

faq.q: 空心菜放冰箱可以放多久？
faq.a: 裝袋放在 4 °C 以下大約 3～5 天。它怕冷，所以冷藏並不會給它像涼房那樣的壽命。

faq.q: 空心菜冰過為什麼變黑？
faq.a: 它在大約 10～14 °C 以下就會出現低溫傷害，葉和莖都會變深。那是冷害，不是一般的腐壞。
沒有已發表的期限，生凍效果也差。建議先炒熟，把菜吃掉。
不要。下鍋前才洗；表面帶水會讓切口更快變黏。
